title: Jev names a primary and a backup, and a run that cannot start on the first runs on the second
name: backup
description: `modelQuestion`/`jevChoice` in packages/core/src/jev.ts ask Jev for one name. Ask for two: `model` and `backup`, the backup on a different host than the primary whenever the candidate list has one (say so in the question text, and reject a backup equal to the primary). When the primary is on the `openrouter` host, the backup is a `claude` or `codex` model, never another `openrouter` one: free models share an upstream pool and rate-limit together. Carry both into the run record — packages/schema/src/run.ts gains `backup: string | null` and `ran: 'primary' | 'backup'` (schema version bump per the schema's own rules, migration for old records defaulting to `ran: 'primary'`). In `dispatch()`: `checkHost` and the availability probe (host-avail) on the primary; a refusal switches to the backup's line before the worktree; and if the primary's process exits before its first tool line with a limit/auth classification (`limitSpent` from host-avail — for `openrouter`, a 429 left after the loop's bounded retry), the same worktree is re-run on the backup once and the record says `ran: 'backup'` with the primary's reason in a `fellBack` field. No backup available → today's refusal, unchanged. `sober status`, `sober logs` header and the dashboard run line (node sober-status-sober-logs-and-the-run-pane-0o4s renders them) read the new fields; keep that node's surface change out of here, only make the data available. Tests: jev.test.ts for the two-name question, the same-host rejection and the openrouter → claude/codex rule; dispatch.test.ts for switch-before-start and fall-after-start with a fake host that prints the captured limit text; schema migration test.
